description: Open-weight decision models (0.6B & 1.7B) built on Qwen3 with learned decision tokens: runtime answer choices are scored via a masked softmax over decision-token slots, returned as full answer distributions.
features: Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B causal base + rank-16 LoRA adapter + 256 learned decision tokens (per HF blog)
Up to 255 candidates per question; one token reserved as null slot
Readout: masked softmax over presented decision tokens mapped back to candidate order
Trained on 80,000 base decision examples + 50,000 from additional decision-task families (per model card via blog)
Typed decision API (choice/score/noul) via Jev-compatible /v1/systemone server
name: Bosun v3.1

description: Open-weight 32B long-CoT reasoning model trained to replicate o1-style deliberate reasoning for complex decision tasks.
features: Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct base; SFT on 17K verified reasoning traces from QwQ-32B-Preview
Trained for under $450 (vendor-reported)
Card-reported evals: Math500 82.4, AIME2024 43.3, GPQA-Diamond 56.8 (vendor-reported)
Code open-source at NovaSky-AI/SkyThought
name: Sky-T1-32B-Preview

description: Open-weight evaluator LLMs (7B & 8x7B) for judging and verifying decisions: direct Likert assessment and pairwise ranking.
features: Prometheus 2 8x7B: 0.6-0.7 Pearson correlation with GPT-4-1106 on VicunaBench/MT-Bench/FLASK (per repo README)
72-85% agreement with human judgments on pairwise benchmarks (per repo README)
7B variant runs in 16GB VRAM with ~80% of the 8x7B's eval performance (per repo README)
Pip-installable as prometheus-eval; Apache-2.0 license
name: Prometheus 2

description: Open reasoning model trained with large-scale RL (GRPO): the deliberative substrate behind many decision benchmarks and distilled decision fine-tunes.
features: 671B MoE (37B active), 128K context, MIT license
R1-Zero trained with pure RL, no SFT; reasoning behaviors emerged from verifiable rewards
Per README, matches o1-level performance on math/code/reasoning
Listed here once for its decision role; full coverage in awesome-flagship-llms
name: DeepSeek-R1

description: Game-theoretic benchmark for LLM strategic reasoning: 10 games in a language-driven OpenSpiel environment.
features: 10 games: tic-tac-toe, Connect-4, breakthrough, nim, blind auction, Kuhn poker, liar's dice, negotiation, pig, iterated prisoner's dilemma
NeurIPS 2024
Per authors: LLMs fail in complete/deterministic games but are competitive in probabilistic ones
HF leaderboard at huggingface.co/spaces/GTBench/GTBench; repo github.com/danyflores7/gtbench
name: GTBench

description: Cross-domain strategic-reasoning benchmark: 9 game environments chosen to resist pretraining contamination.
features: Each of 9 games targets a distinct strategy-game reasoning skill
Evaluated GPT-3/GPT-4 base plus CoT and Reasoning-Via-Planning scaffolds
Per authors: no tested model matched human performance; GPT-4 performed below random action at worst
Scaffolding helped but not to human level; code at github.com/Joshuaclymer/GameBench
name: GameBench

description: Systematic and Tuneable Evaluation of Economic Rationality: fine-grained 'elements' of rational decision-making with a STEER report card.
features: Built from a survey of the economics literature on rational decision-making
Large-scale experiment across 14 different LLMs
Analyzes the impact of model size on rational behavior
Covers risk, time, social preference, and strategic choice elements
name: STEER

description: Dynamic benchmark of LLM rationality via competitive economics games (beauty contests, second-price auctions) with well-defined Nash equilibria.
features: NeurIPS 2024
Tests deviation from Nash equilibrium, strategic reasoning from game history, instruction-following
9 LLMs across 150 independent sessions; per authors all models deviated from NE even when told opponents were rational (Claude 2, GPT-4 deviated least)
Pip-installable package (econarena) with example scripts
name: EconArena

description: 134 choose-your-own-adventure games (500K+ scenarios) measuring trade-offs between reward maximization and ethical behavior.
features: ICML 2023 Oral
Scenario labels produced by LMs (GPT-4), reported to outperform human annotators
Per authors: tension between maximizing reward and behaving ethically; LM-based steering achieved Pareto safety+capability improvements
Repo: github.com/aypan17/machiavelli (via secondary source)
name: MACHIAVELLI

description: Long-horizon interactive decision-making for LLM/VLM agents: BabyAI, TextWorld, Crafter, Baba Is AI, MiniHack, NetHack (10^1 to 10^5 steps).
features: ICLR 2025
Procedurally generated environments resist memorization
Tests navigation, exploration, resource management, credit assignment, long-term planning
Per authors: LLMs can answer mechanics questions yet fail to apply them in practice; repo github.com/balrog-ai/BALROG
name: BALROG

description: Extensible planning benchmark on International Planning Competition domains (Blocksworld etc.): plan generation and reasoning about change.
features: NeurIPS 2023 Datasets & Benchmarks
Per authors: LLM plan generation 'falls quite short' even of SOTA models
Community leaderboard in repo (github.com/karthikv792/LLMs-Planning): reasoning models (R1, o1) later reached ~99% on Blocksworld but collapse on Mystery Blocksworld
Companion critique 'On the planning abilities of LLMs' (NeurIPS 2023 Spotlight)
name: PlanBench

description: Foundational sycophancy evaluation: do assistants agree with the user's beliefs over the evidence?
features: arXiv Oct 2023
Five SOTA assistants exhibited sycophancy across four free-form tasks (per authors)
Matching user views increased human preference; optimizing against preference models sometimes sacrificed truthfulness
Follow-ups SycEval (AIES 2025) and SYCON-Bench (EMNLP 2025) via secondary sources only
name: SycophancyEval

description: Bargaining formalized as an asymmetric incomplete-information game, benchmarked on real Amazon price-history data.
features: arXiv 2024
Playing buyer is much harder than seller; larger model size did not effectively improve buyer performance
Proposed OG-Narrator raised buyer deal rates from 26.67% to 88.88% and profits ~10x across baselines (per authors)
name: Bargaining Abilities of LLMs

description: Utility-theory quantification of LLM economic biases (loss aversion, anchoring, framing) against perfect-rationality and human benchmarks.
features: COLM 2024
Current LLMs are neither fully human-like nor fully economicus-like (per authors)
Models struggle to maintain consistent economic behavior across settings
Framework also measures effects of interventions like prompting on biases
name: LLM economicus?

description: Community benchmark: 1,500 paired baseline-vs-biased cases measuring 30 cognitive biases across 7 categories, with a standardized 0-100 LCB Score.
features: MIT license; categories: decision-making (sunk cost, framing, loss aversion), judgment & estimation, probability, social cognition, LLM-specific (sycophancy, position, verbosity), information processing, memory
Self-reported leaderboard (Mar 2026): GPT-4o 83.8, GPT-4o-mini 80.3, Gemini 2.5 Flash 77.2, Claude Sonnet 4.6 69.0 - author claims, not independent results
Each case has baseline and biased prompts plus a scoring spec (anchor-pull index, decision consistency, Bayesian calibration)
Tiny project (1 star, 5 commits, created 2026-03-18); companion paper still 'forthcoming on arXiv' - treat accordingly
name: LCB-Bench

description: Large-scale study: 8 cognitive biases across 45 LLMs with 220 hand-curated decision scenarios (2.8M+ responses).
features: arXiv Sep 2025
Bias-consistent behavior in 17.8-57.3% of instances (per authors)
Models >32B params reduced bias in ~39.5% of cases; detailed prompts reduced most biases up to ~14.9%
Psychologist-collaborated scenario templates covering anchoring, availability, confirmation, framing, interpretation, overattribution, prospect theory, representativeness
name: The Bias is in the Details

description: Revealed-preference (GARP) measurement of GPT's economic rationality across 10,000 budgetary decision tasks in risk, time, social, and food domains.
features: GPT-3.5-Turbo scored higher on rationality than 347 human subjects and human literature benchmarks (per authors)
Rationality robust to temperature and demographic framing, sensitive to price framing and discrete-choice formats
GPT's estimated preference parameters were more homogeneous than humans'
name: Economic rationality of GPT

description: Open benchmark of how accurately, quickly, and cheaply language models make bounded decisions on real data.
features: Corpus bench-v4: 1,071 rows across 35 tasks and 11 use cases sampled from 36 public datasets
Reports accuracy with 95% CIs, calibration, latency, token usage, and cost
12-model results published 2026-09-23 with leaderboard at decisionbench.ai
MIT license. Note: distinct from Hanno Labs' DecisionBench - a naming overlap, different projects
name: DecisionBench

description: Interactive multi-agent negotiation testbed: scorable, multi-issue, semantically rich games measuring cooperation, competition, and maliciousness.
features: NeurIPS 2024 Datasets & Benchmarks paper: 'Cooperation, Competition, and Maliciousness: LLM-Stakeholders Interactive Negotiation'
Agents need arithmetic, inference, exploration, and planning in dynamic multi-turn setups
Per authors: GPT-3.5 and small models mostly fail; GPT-4 and SoTA large models still underperform in adversarial, noisy, competitive games
MIT license; ships all games, paper logs, simulation and evaluation code
name: LLM-Deliberation

description: Platform for evaluating and probing LLM negotiation: buy-sell, ultimatum, and resource-exchange games.
features: Paper: arXiv 2402.05863 ('How Well Can LLMs Negotiate?')
All tested models showed cognitive biases (anchoring, framing)
Striking finding: an LLM improved its own payoff ~20% by feigning desperation (per secondary survey)
Repo currently being refactored (work in progress); paper experiments on the paper_experiment_code branch; MIT
name: NegotiationArena

description: 2x2 game benchmark evaluating LLMs in sequential, parallel, and nested game formats.
features: arXiv 2024
Per paper: o1-mini 66.6%/60.0%/70.0% vs gpt-4o 50.0%/35.0%/70.0% across the three forms
Single-sourced (arXiv PDF only) - less established than GTBench
name: TMGBench

description: Deliberate decision-making at inference time: explore multiple reasoning paths, self-evaluate choices, lookahead/backtrack via BFS/DFS.
features: NeurIPS 2023
Game of 24: 74% success vs 4% for GPT-4 with CoT prompting (per abstract)
Also evaluated on Creative Writing and Mini Crosswords; repo published with all prompts
Authors: Princeton / Google DeepMind; canonical reference implementation
name: Tree of Thoughts

description: Thoughts modeled as an arbitrary graph (vertices=thoughts, edges=dependencies) with generate/aggregate/refine operations.
features: AAAI 2024
Sorting quality improved 62% over Tree of Thoughts while cutting cost >31% (per abstract)
Thought aggregation and feedback loops not expressible in trees; CoT/ToT are special cases of GoT
name: Graph of Thoughts

description: Language agents with verbal reinforcement learning: reflect on task feedback, store reflections in episodic memory, improve across trials without weight updates.
features: NeurIPS 2023
91% pass@1 on HumanEval vs ~80% GPT-4 at the time (per abstract)
Evaluated on sequential decision-making (AlfWorld), coding, and language reasoning
Actor/Evaluator/Self-Reflection triad
name: Reflexion

description: Reasoning+Acting: interleave Thought/Action/Observation so reasoning grounds decision choices in real tool feedback - the decision loop under modern agents.
features: ICLR 2023
Evaluated on HotpotQA, FEVER, ALFWorld, WebShop
Reported ALFWorld success 71% vs 22% imitation-learning baseline (secondary source)
Foundational to LangChain/AutoGPT-style decision loops; reference implementation at github.com/ysymyth/ReAct (not verified here)
name: ReAct

description: Round-table consensus among diverse LLMs: multiple discussion rounds with confidence-weighted voting toward a better consensus decision.
features: ACL 2024
Beats prior single- and multi-agent baselines by up to 11.4% (per abstract)
Outperforms GPT-4 on three datasets (per abstract)
Model diversity (API, open-source, domain-specific) shown critical
name: ReConcile

description: Layered architecture: proposer LLM layers generate diverse candidate answers, an aggregator synthesizes them into a single decision/output.
features: ICLR 2025
65.1% on AlpacaEval 2.0 with open models only, beating GPT-4 Omni's 57.5% (per repo README)
No fine-tuning - pure prompting; concept called 'collaborativeness' of LLMs
Apache-2.0 license
name: Mixture-of-Agents

description: Multi-agent LLM financial decision framework: analyst team, bull/bear researcher debate, trader, risk-manager agents, portfolio-manager final decision.
features: v0.5.2 (Sept 2026); LangGraph orchestration with deepThink/quickThink models
Bull/bear debate reduces one-sided reasoning
Research-only: no live order execution; not financial, investment, or trading advice
Apache-2.0 license
name: TradingAgents

description: Program (don't prompt) LMs: declarative signatures plus algorithmic optimizers (MIPRO) to compile high-quality multi-step decision pipelines.
features: MIT license; ~38.4K stars, 4.7K commits, 113 releases (per GitHub, Sept 2026)
Composable modules: ChainOfThought, ReAct, ProgramOfThought
Evaluation-driven prompt/weight optimization instead of hand-engineering
Docs at dspy.ai
name: DSPy

description: Retrieval-augmented multi-agent prediction-market simulator: binary/categorical/scalar markets priced by Hanson's LMSR.
features: Flask + SQLAlchemy
Supports binary, categorical, scalar, grouped, and conditional events
Optional Tavily evidence retrieval and OpenAI-compatible LLM providers for evidence appraisal and decisions
Local demo/research prototype with virtual cash and leaderboard scoring
name: ForecastArena

description: Mechanism-design research tool: simulates agent organizations with private beliefs and compares a Decision Market vs a VCG-inspired auction.
features: LLM-powered diverse agent profile generator
Core LMSR prediction-market AMM plus VCGR mechanism
FastAPI backend and Jekyll web UI
Multi-action conditional decision markets
name: DMsim

description: LMSR prediction-market simulation engine with truthful/noisy/LLM-based/robust/adversarial agents for stress-testing decisions under uncertainty.
features: Reports mean wealth, worst outcomes, and CVaR tail-risk metrics
LLM strategy agents via Gemini (with API fallback)
Jupyter experiment notebooks with visualizations
Belief-misspecification and adversary on/off ablations
name: prediction-market-lmsr

description: Python library implementing 70+ Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis methods (AHP, TOPSIS, ELECTRE, PROMETHEE, VIKOR, fuzzy variants) with LLM result interpretation.
features: By Valdecy Pereira et al., Federal Fluminense University; published in Journal of Modelling in Management
Companion paper 'Enhancing Decision Analysis with a Large Language Model: pyDecision' (arXiv 2404.06370, via secondary source)
Extensive Colab demos; LLM integration covers interpreting and comparing method outcomes
Active through 2026-06
name: pyDecision

description: Multi-agent referee team: diverse role-prompted LLMs debate and judge generated responses (the debate-based judging pattern).
features: Paper: arXiv 2308.07201 ('ChatEval: Towards Better LLM-based Evaluators through Multi-Agent Debate')
Role-prompt diversity shown essential; same-role prompts degrade performance (per secondary source)
Apache-2.0 license
Evaluation-focused: included for the debate-judge pattern, not as a decision-support tool per se
name: ChatEval

description: Large Language Models as Optimizers: a meta-prompt carries a score-sorted trajectory of past solutions; the model proposes better ones.
features: ICLR 2024
Demonstrated on linear regression, TSP, and prompt/instruction optimization
OPRO prompts beat human-designed prompts by up to 8% on GSM8K and up to 50% on Big-Bench Hard (per authors)
Optimizers tested: PaLM 2-L, text-bison, GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4
name: OPRO

description: Casts RL as conditional sequence modeling: a causally-masked Transformer conditioned on desired return outputs actions directly.
features: NeurIPS 2021 (Berkeley / FAIR / Google Brain)
No value functions or policy gradients
Matched or exceeded SOTA model-free offline RL baselines on Atari, OpenAI Gym, Key-to-Door (per authors)
Pre-LLM template for RL-as-sequence-modeling; code at github.com/kzl/decision-transformer (via secondary source)
name: Decision Transformer

description: N LLM instances answer independently, then see each other's reasoning and revise over rounds toward a consensus answer ('society of minds').
features: ICML 2024 (arXiv May 2023)
Improves mathematical/strategic reasoning and factuality vs single-instance baselines; reduces (not eliminates) hallucinations
Model-agnostic; works on black-box models with identical prompts
~9 calls per question; convergence does not guarantee correctness
name: Multiagent Debate

description: Teach the model the safety spec text directly; train it to reason over specs in chain-of-thought before answering.
features: OpenAI, Dec 2024
SFT on spec-referencing CoTs via context distillation, then process+outcome-based RL
Used to align OpenAI's o-series models
Per authors pushed the Pareto frontier: jailbreak robustness + lower over-refusal + better OOD generalization; no human-written CoTs needed
name: Deliberative Alignment

description: GPT-3 finetuned to emit verbalized confidence ('90% confidence') alongside answers - well-calibrated without logits.
features: TMLR 2022 (venue via secondary source)
Introduced the CalibratedMath suite for calibration testing
Verbalized calibration generalized under distribution shift, beating the answer-logit baseline
Sensitivity tracks the model's own uncertainty, not imitation of human examples
name: Teaching Models to Express Their Uncertainty in Words

description: Foundational study of LLMs as evaluators: GPT-4 judge matches human preferences at ~80% agreement.
features: NeurIPS 2023 Datasets & Benchmarks
Introduced MT-Bench (80 multi-turn questions) and Chatbot Arena
Documents position bias, verbosity bias, self-enhancement bias, and limited reasoning ability as judge failure modes
Code/data: github.com/lm-sys/FastChat; 3K expert votes + 30K human-preference conversations released
name: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge

description: Survey organizing agentic-LLM literature into reasoning, acting, and interacting.
features: arXiv 2025
Reasoning strand explicitly 'aims to improve decision making'
Notes synergies: retrieval enables tool use, reflection improves multi-agent collaboration
Flags real-world deployment risks: safety, liability, security
name: Agentic LLMs survey

description: Foundations of decision-focused / predict-then-optimize learning: train predictors to minimize downstream decision regret, not standalone prediction error.
features: Comprehensive arXiv survey (v4)
Covers gradient-based vs gradient-free DFL methods and smooth surrogates for discrete decisions
Central challenge: differentiating through argmin and discontinuous mappings
Foundational method paper: Wilder et al., 'Melding the Data-Decisions Pipeline' (AAAI 2019) - arXiv ID not verified here
name: Decision-Focused Learning survey

description: Framework + evaluation of LLMs on multi-criteria decision-making problems against human-expert ground truth.
features: arXiv 2025
Open models plus Claude/ChatGPT reached only ~60% accuracy vs expert ground truth on 3 applications
CoT/few-shot raised accuracy to ~70%; LoRA finetuning pushed ~95% with trivial cross-model differences (per authors)
Bridges classical MCDM with LLM decision-making
name: One for All (MCDM)

description: Finetunes pretrained LLMs on oracle-labeled trajectories for few-shot decision-making in MDPs, POMDPs, and ambiguous POMDPs.
features: arXiv 2026
Finetuned attention layer interpreted as implicitly estimating optimal Q-functions from in-context data
Derives an end-to-end suboptimality bound separating in-context estimation error from training-length bias
Largest gains in long-horizon, partially observed, model-ambiguous settings; motivated by healthcare offline data
name: LLMs for Sequential Decision-Making

description: Uses an LLM as the decision-making 'brain' for autonomous driving, with language as the decision interface.
features: arXiv 2023
Evaluated on safety, efficiency, generalizability, and interoperability in driving scenarios
LLM decision-making with interpretability suited to regulatory scrutiny
Addresses the black-box nature of learning-based autonomous-driving systems
name: LanguageMPC

description: Game-theoretic workflows guiding LLM reasoning in strategic decision-making and negotiation games (Nash-equilibrium computation, rational choices under uncertainty).
features: Per authors: LLMs deviate from rational strategies as payoff matrices deepen
Workflows markedly improve optimal-strategy identification and near-optimal allocations in negotiations
Also tested whether adopting the workflow is itself a rational meta-strategy
Code at github.com/Wenyueh/game_theory
name: Game-theoretic LLM workflows

description: How epistemic markers ('I'm sure', 'I think') in prompts affect LM accuracy: high-certainty expressions reduced accuracy 7% vs low-certainty ones.
features: arXiv 2023 (v2, Nov 2023)
50 epistemic markers injected into QA prompts; accuracies varied >80%
Factive verbs hurt performance, evidentials helped (per authors)
Pretraining analysis suggests mimicking language use rather than reflecting true epistemic uncertainty
name: Navigating the Grey Area
DecisionBench (Hanno Labs)
description: Open decision-model benchmark (MTEB-inspired): frozen tasks with row-level evidence and a community result record across typed decision primitives.
features: DecisionBench 1.0: 43 tasks, 23,900 English rows, 28 domains (per launch blog)
Standard applied suite: 22,700 rows; separate 1,200-row reasoning track (multistep, numerical, evidence-heavy)
Primary score all-row accuracy; also reports coverage, ECE, NLL; unsupported/failed responses count as misses
Frozen tasks, pinned dataset revision; results repo + leaderboard; distinct from Atlan AI's DecisionBench
